quality.scope: Exactness qualifies these optimizations against the existing quantized implementation, not unquantized upstream parity. Earlier C2/4/6/8 and cancellation qualification is retained above; no duplicate full matrix here.

rejected: Generic per-K partial-tile guards and separate tail launches were slower.
LDS-only barriers, W8A8 barrier changes and cached-word rotations did not improve complete kernels.
BFI word selection was slower than retained conditional selects.
Smaller selector histograms regressed deep rows.
Selector dot-product ILP groups2/4/8/16 remained exact but did not improve speed.
Rolling boundary convolution improved some isolated shapes but not full-model time; removed entirely, including the short-row specialization.
Full/partial outer expert-loop hoisting was slower, especially wider tiles. Four-phase constant code indices improved the micro/profile but not full HTTP enough to justify retaining them.
Routing partial tiles with no wholly empty16-token subtile to the unguarded path remained exact but was slower in complete projection/convolution controls. No production change or extra model sweep.
limitations: One sample per HTTP control, with a targeted reverse d0 pair for the marginal rejected loop. Small differences are observations, not confidence bounds.
The first mixed-MTP d32K baseline was unusually slow (1388.03tok/s); other preceding controls were1465–1474. Do not attribute the entire difference to this change.
Default-sampled warm-up tg8 varies; only warmed tg128 is a throughput comparison.
The earlier first-decode latency investigation remains inconclusive as documented above.
Neither sustained1700tok/s nor flat d0–d128K performance is established.
